Test image: A mango leaf with a grayish-green, dusty/powdery coating covering most of the surface. There are scattered dark spots and a white-gray powdery substance visible across the blade. The leaf appears dull and coated rather than having discrete brown lesions or dead tips.

Key features: widespread powdery/dusty white-gray coating, scattered small dark specks, overall matte texture.

Now let me view one reference from each class.
Strong match — same grayish-green leaf with powdery white patches and dark speckles scattered across the surface. Now check the other classes.
Sooty mould shows darker, sooty/black patches rather than white powdery coating. Less similar to the test image. Now check Anthracnose and Die_Back.

Anthracnose shows brown/tan leaf with necrotic lesions — not matching. Die_Back shows completely desiccated brown tissue — not matching. Powdery_Mildew is the clear frontrunner. Let me use remaining budget to confirm and check Sooty_Mould more carefully.
Another strong Powdery_Mildew match. Let me check Sooty_Mould further and one more Powdery_Mildew reference.

Sooty_Mould shows dark brown/black patches concentrated along the midrib — distinct from the test image. The Powdery_Mildew reference here shows the same white-gray powdery patches on green leaf tissue, confirming the match.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: green mango leaf with widespread white-gray powdery coating and scattered dark specks
- Powdery_Mildew refs (14, 24, 164): all show the same grayish-green leaf with white powdery/dusty patches — highly consistent
- Sooty_Mould: darker black sooty deposits, concentrated near midrib — different pattern
- Anthracnose: yellow-brown leaf with brown necrotic lesions — different
- Die_Back: completely desiccated brown tissue — different
